title: How to Remove Holi Colours from Clothes: Simple Laundry Tips
excerpt: How to remove Holi colour stains from clothes with simple laundry steps: what to do first, how to soak and wash, and when to stop and accept a mark.
body:
The secret to removing Holi colours from clothes is to act quickly, use cold water and be patient. Shake off the dry powder, rinse from the back of the fabric, soak, then wash separately, repeating if needed before anything goes in a hot dryer. Here are simple, general laundry tips to help after 22 March 2027, plus honest advice on what to expect.

## The first wash: three simple steps

### Step one: deal with dry powder first

Before any water touches your outfit, get rid of as much dry colour as possible.

- Take the clothes outside and shake them well.
- Gently brush off powder with your hand or a soft brush.
- Do not rub the fabric, as rubbing pushes the colour deeper into the fibres.

Dry gulal on a dry outfit is much easier to remove than wet colour, so this one step makes a real difference.

### Step two: rinse with cold water

Hot water can help some stains set, so stick to cold water at first.

- Turn the garment inside out.
- Rinse under running cold water from the back of the stain, pushing colour out the way it came in.
- Keep rinsing until the water runs mostly clear.

### Step three: soak and wash separately

Soak the garment in cold water with your usual laundry detergent for a while, then wash it on its own or only with other Holi clothes. Coloured water can transfer to other items, so never wash Holi outfits with your regular laundry.

If marks remain, repeat the soak and wash. Several gentle rounds usually work better than one harsh one.

## Choose the method by fabric

| Fabric or garment | Best approach | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| Plain white cotton | Cold rinse, soak with detergent, repeat; dry in sunlight | Hot water before stains lift |
| Block printed cotton | Gentle hand wash in cold water, wash alone | Chlorine bleach, hard scrubbing |
| Embroidered pieces | Turn inside out, hand wash gently, dab stains | Wringing, rubbing the embroidery |
| Organza or Kota Doria dupatta | Soak briefly, swish gently, rinse | Machine wash, scrubbing |
| Denim | Cold rinse, machine wash alone on a cool cycle | Tumble drying with stains |
| Silk or dry-clean only | Take to a professional cleaner | Home soaking |

## Using stain removers safely

If detergent alone is not enough, you can try a stain remover meant for laundry.

- Always read the product label and the garment's care label first.
- Test on a hidden spot, like an inside seam, before using it on a visible area.
- Avoid chlorine bleach on prints, embroidery and coloured fabrics, as it can damage the colours and threads.
- Do not mix different cleaning products.

## Drying: the step people get wrong

Do not put a stained garment in a hot tumble dryer. Heat can fix the remaining colour permanently. Air-dry instead and check the fabric in daylight. If you still see marks, wash again before drying with heat.

White cotton often looks brighter after drying in sunlight. Printed and coloured pieces are better dried in the shade, inside out, to protect their colours.

## Caring for embroidered and block printed outfits

Pieces with handwork need a gentle touch. For something like the [off-white embroidered kurta set with organza dupatta](/products/off-white-embroidered-cotton-flex-kurta-pant-organza-dupatta-set/), turn it inside out, hand wash in cold water and press stains with a cloth rather than scrubbing. Dry flat or on a hanger in the shade.

Hand block printed cotton, such as our [grey block print kurta set with Kota Doria dupatta](/products/grey-hand-block-print-cotton-kurta-pant-kota-doria-dupatta-set/), should be washed separately in cold water, especially for the first few washes.

You can read more about these pieces in our [hand block print](/hand-block-print-kurta-sets/) collection.

## Be realistic, and plan ahead

Some Holi colours are very strong and may not come out completely, however careful you are. That is why many people keep a dedicated Holi outfit. A practical idea is a cotton tunic you can wear with jeans, like the [aqua leaf block print pintuck tunic](/products/aqua-leaf-hand-block-print-cotton-pintuck-tunic-top/), which you will not mind wearing again next year with a few faint marks.

## Frequently asked questions

**Should I use hot or cold water for Holi colour stains?**
Start with cold water. Hot water can help some stains set, so only use warmer water if the care label allows it and the stain has mostly lifted.

**Can I wash Holi clothes with my other laundry?**
No. Wash them separately, as the colour can transfer to other clothes in the wash.

**Is it safe to use bleach on Holi stains?**
Avoid chlorine bleach on printed, embroidered or coloured fabrics. Check the care label and test any stain remover on a hidden spot first.

**What if the colour does not come out fully?**
Some colours are very stubborn. Repeat gentle washes, and if marks remain, keep the piece as your dedicated Holi outfit.
